summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for tachycardia, weakness, and diarrhea. He was found to have Strep gallolyticus sepsis and recurrent Clostridium difficile infection. IV and oral vancomycin were initiated, with negative follow-up blood cultures. His tachycardia resolved with volume repletion and restarting carvedilol and diltiazem. Bilateral knee pain prompted X-rays, revealing a possible lucent lesion in the right knee, raising concern for myeloma progression. His oncology team decided to switch from pomalidomide and cyclophosphamide to ixazomib outpatient. He received transfusions for pancytopenia and completed a dose of Velcade inpatient. An echocardiogram showed no endocarditis. He improved clinically, with stable vital signs and no diarrhea in hospital, and was discharged home with home IV antibiotics and close oncology follow-up.
